works.name: PPTX Builder
works.tech_stack: Python (python-pptx, Pillow, PyMuPDF, pdf2image, pillow-heif, tqdm)
works.short_description: A local-first converter that turns PDFs and image folders into clean, size-controlled PowerPoint presentations without uploading a single file.
substantive_description: Online converters require you to upload your documents and then hand back fragile "editable" results that fall apart on anything complex. PPTX Builder refuses both: it processes entirely on your own machine and produces consistent raster output you control. It renders PDFs or organizes image folders into one-slide-per-page decks with configurable DPI and encoder, a range of aspect ratios and paper sizes, and fit-or-fill placement, handling batch and recursive folders. Output size is the lever most converters hide: PPTX Builder exposes both halves of it, so a 43-page deck is 14 MB at the defaults or 83 MB in lossless PNG at 300 DPI, and the choice is yours rather than the tool's. The primary interface is a pip-installable Python CLI, with an optional Gradio web UI and a Docker deployment carrying environment-variable limits for self-hosted instances. The problem it solves is small and common — private, predictable document-to-slides conversion — and it solves it without asking you to trust a server.

Python 3.8+ with python-pptx, Pillow, PyMuPDF, pdf2image, pillow-heif, and tqdm; optional Gradio web UI; Docker-deployable with poppler-utils. Published to PyPI as sageframe-pptx-builder (v0.3.0), which made the page encoder configurable — `--format`, `--quality`, and `PPTX_FORMAT`/`PPTX_QUALITY`/`PPTX_DPI` — and moved the defaults to 200 DPI JPEG q85. A capped public demo runs at pptx.sageframe.net; an uncapped instance runs on the homelab at pptx-full.sageframe.net.

state.last: **ho-01 closed, merged, published, and deployed twice.** Output format and quality are threaded through the pipeline, CLI, interactive prompt, and Gradio UI; the hardcoded `fmt="png"` literal is gone. Bare `pptx-builder -i deck.pdf` produces 200 DPI JPEG q85 — 13.8 MB on a 43-page deck against 83.1 MB for the previous 300 DPI PNG default. Added `--format`, `--quality`, `PPTX_FORMAT`, `PPTX_QUALITY`, `PPTX_DPI`, `PPTX_MAX_QUALITY`. 136 tests, coverage 100%, black/mypy clean, flake8 identical to baseline. Merged as `3583e91`; **0.3.0 published to PyPI** via the `v0.3.0` tag. Also fixed a latent Dockerfile defect (`0a66448`): the dependency-priming layer installed a stub `__init__.py` and setuptools then skipped re-copying real sources because `COPY` preserves older mtimes — pip reported the right version while the package exposed nothing. Now cleared before reinstall with a build-time import assertion. **Two instances live:** the capped public demo (miseba, `pptx.sageframe.net`, 20 MB/20 files/20 pages/300 DPI) and a new uncapped practitioner instance (tenzo, `pptx-full.sageframe.net`, 2000 MB/500 files/1200 DPI/∞ pages, scratch on `rpool/sage/tenzo/pptx-builder`, LAN-only, on Flame). Deployment tracked in sageframe-config `8125b1d`.
state.next: unset; practitioner to point. Candidates: reconstruct the absent Kamae chain (K1/K2/K4), or give `ho-process/` a remote so the Kamae documents are backed up.
